subject: Telemetry & vendor data handling — scope, retention, and next steps
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Telemetry & vendor data handling — scope, retention, and next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — great conversation. Per our discovery, I summarized the outstanding items we need to lock down to qualify the integration and give your security team the artifacts they requested. Quick recap + asks below.

Summary of what we heard (FinLytics):
- Use case: real-time assistant for customer support, some analytics for usage patterns.
- Cloud: currently on AWS (us-west-2) and plan to route traffic through Marketplace SaaS integration initially.
- Telemetry vendors: currently using CloudBridge Analytics for event telemetry; will potentially add a managed log shipper.

Items we need from you (and a few clarifications from our side):
1) PII scope — which fields in prompts or user metadata do you consider PII? Examples to confirm: full name, email address, phone, SSN, payment tokens. If you can paste a short sample (sanitized) row that helps.
2) Data sent to Redwood — at a high level, does FinLytics send raw prompt text and model output to analytics vendors, or do you hash/strip sensitive fields before shipping?
3) Retention windows — current retention for logs, analytics, and audit trails (e.g., 90 days vs 12 months). Any regulatory retention needs?
4) Logging & access controls — who at FinLytics should be able to view raw prompts/outputs in logs and which roles need redaction?
5) Subprocessors — a list of telemetry/analytics vendors we should disclose to your security team (you mentioned CloudBridge; any others?).
6) Marketplace flow — confirm whether you plan to transact via AWS Marketplace (we can support both SaaS Metering and direct procurement). If Marketplace, who will be the billing entity?

Attachments: I attached a simple vendor questions spreadsheet and a blank dataflow diagram that would help your security team map the flow.

Next steps I propose:
- You share the PII scope and vendor list (by EOD Wed).
- We provide a recommended retention baseline and a redaction pattern (by Fri) + short security pre-qualification artifact from our side.
- 30-minute follow-up (technical + security) the week of Apr 25 to align on redaction and Marketplace contract path.

If anything above is inaccurate, please flag. Happy to hop on a quick call.

Best,
Jasmine
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: vendor-telemetry-questions.xlsx (sheet: telemetry_scope)
Attachment: finlytics-dataflow-diagram.pdf

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finlytics.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Aaron Park <aaron.park@cloudbridge.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry & vendor data handling — scope, retention, and next steps

Thanks, Jasmine — good notes and appreciate the clear asks. Answers inline below.

1) PII scope: we treat these as PII: full name, email, phone, postal address, SSN, and payment card last4 when associated with transaction context. We do not expect Redwood to process raw payment card PANs.

2) Data sent today: for analytics we currently send prompt text + event metadata to CloudBridge. Prompt text is not consistently redacted today, which is on our backlog. For billing/usage we send token counts and anonymous user identifiers (hashed user_id). We can provide a sanitized sample.

3) Retention: operational logs ~90 days; analytics/aggregates ~12 months; audit logs for security ~24 months. Regulatory note: we have a small EU customer base with a contractual 6 month retention cap for certain accounts (we can flag those).

4) Logging & access: raw prompts currently visible to our data-science and platform-eng teams, gated by role-based access. We need options to prevent exposure of raw prompts to 3rd-party vendors unless explicitly allowed (e.g., aggregated telemetry only).

5) Subprocessors: primary telemetry vendor is CloudBridge (contact Aaron Park cc'd). We also use S3 (AWS) for intermediate storage and Splunk for aggregated logs right now.

6) Marketplace flow: yes, plan is AWS Marketplace SaaS. Billing entity is FinLytics (they will buy through their AWS account).

Two asks for Redwood: 1) Can Redwood provide a recommended retention default and easy-to-toggle redaction options (e.g., strip emails & numbers from prompts) and 2) what third-party sharing controls are configurable (disable telemetry export to CloudBridge, route telemetry to customer-owned S3/VPC)?

Happy to take a 30-minute call. Wed/Thu afternoons next week look good for us.

Thanks,
Olivia
Head of Product Operations | FinLytics

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finlytics.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 18:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry & vendor data handling — scope, retention, and next steps

Jasmine / Olivia — thanks for the details. A few notes from Redwood side that will help speed the security review and procurement: 

- Retention options: we can support configurable retention per-customer: 0 / 7 / 30 / 90 / 365 / custom days. Default for Hosted is 90 days for raw telemetry; Dedicated/Private deployments can have retention disabled or routed to customer-controlled storage.
- Redaction: we offer a pre-processing pipeline that can remove or hash identifiable tokens in prompts before they are stored or forwarded to telemetry vendors. We can share patterns (regexes) for email, phone, credit-card, and SSN.
- Subprocessor controls: we publish a subprocessor list and can provide a tailored disclosure for FinLytics. For Hosted customers who want zero third-party sharing, we recommend Dedicated or Private where telemetry forwarding can be switched off and logs can be kept in a customer VPC/S3.
- Marketplace: AWS Marketplace SaaS flow is supported. For vendor disclosure, we'll list CloudBridge, Splunk (if we integrate), and AWS services as subprocessors in the DPA appendix.

Marissa — can you take point on assembling a concise security pre-qualification (SOC 2 scope, retention options, where telemetry is stored, KMS/Key control options) and the recommended redaction patterns? Please include a short note on how we handle model prompt caching (KV cache retention) and whether we persist prompt contexts outside ephemeral memory.

Proposed next steps:
1) FinLytics sends sanitized sample and final list of telemetry vendors (by Wed Apr 21).
2) Marissa pulls pre-qual artifacts and redaction patterns (target Thu Apr 22).
3) Jasmine schedules 30-min call week of Apr 25 to finalize Marketplace procurement path and retention settings.

I suggest we include a short agenda on the call: a) clarify dataflow and redaction choices, b) choose retention defaults per dataset type (prompts, outputs, logs), c) confirm Marketplace billing path, d) timeline for vendor gating (if any).

Ben
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>

Perfect — thanks everyone. Olivia, can you drop the sanitized prompt sample and full vendor list by EOD Wed Apr 21? I'll send a calendar invite for a 30-minute slot on Apr 26 at 10:00am PT (tentative) — please confirm availability.

Marissa — assigning the pre-qualification artifact to you per Ben's note. Please include:
- SOC 2 coverage summary (controls that touch telemetry),
- KMS/HSM options and our default key policies,
- retention toggles and how to configure them in the Console,

I'll also attach the vendor questions spreadsheet populated with the items we discussed and include a HubSpot link for the deal (RDW-4871).

Thanks — looking forward to closing next steps.

Jasmine
